verdicts.note: Twenty years in the Clerk's Office, ten as elected clerk [S1], re-elected unopposed in 2022 [S4], and running on the modernization record of her last term [S1][S2]. No outsider element. -2 high holds. S2 could be added to the citations for the 'record of modernizing' clause, but S1 alone supports it.

Attacked from both sides. Toward +: she is a challenger on her first run who has never held office [S3] and proposes changes (published fee schedules, a patron feedback system, employer jury outreach) [S2]. Toward -: 18 years of county employment, 14 in the very office she seeks [S1], and she asks for the job on that experience, not on outsider change; her proposals are service improvements, not a renewal pitch. Neither pole fits; 0 medium holds and still marks the contrast with Cross's -2.

note: Missing scores considered and not proposed: there is no evidence on taxes, spending, housing, safety, climate or reform for either candidate. The office is ministerial and both dossiers' scoring notes say so. Munsch's employer outreach to limit jury service's economic impact [S2] and Cross's statement that the office does not make economic policy [S2] imply no axis direction. Display review: office_does matches contest S1 and S2. race_blurb matches contest S1-S3 (primary 2,153 to 2,098) and is neutral. Cross: summary and three highlights match S1, S2, S5 and S6. Munsch: summary and three highlights match S1, S2, S4 and S5. 'Mostly her own money' is accurate but thin (about $4,000 of $7,529 [S5]); 'about half her own money' would be more precise.
